findings.issue: P123.77 (fix P123-R25) was asked to RUN prove-gates for the lmd9 red row and the lmd10 allow row from a committed tree and record the outcome. Its filed outcome says 'prove-gates not run, per the order', and the diff only changes the planted row's expected case from lmd9 to lmd1 plus a comment. Nothing in the diff or the filed return shows either row going red or green. The lmd1 retarget is a reading, not an observation: the planted text 'the bottom layer holds `_doctor_report` for the collector' is an absolute ordinal followed by an ordinary word, which test__deps.py:652-662 (lmd11) covers on synthetic input, while whether the shipped-tree case lmd1 turns red on that plant is unmeasured. The lmd10 allow row (prove-gates.py:1596-1601, dropping the complement lookahead) is likewise unmeasured. A prove-gates row never seen red is the class this repo's CLAUDE.md warns about.
findings.resolution: From a committed clean tree run `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --only layer_mention_drift` (or the `--only` spelling the tool takes) and record the exit code and per-row verdicts for the plant row (expect lmd1 red) and the lmd10 allow row (expect lmd10 red). If the plant row does not go red under lmd1, retarget it to the case that does.

findings.issue: P123.1: the empty plan (phases: []) is written to disk first and removed again only when the body returns non-zero or raises in-process. The index lock guards writers, not readers, so for the body's duration a hook or status read can see a plan with no phases (which moves the plan gate's tier from 'no manifest' to 'manifest, nothing running'). A kill -9 or power loss between the write and the body's own write leaves that empty plan behind, and the next add-phase then takes the existing-plan path silently. The window is short and the leftover is valid, so this is not a correctness failure.
findings.resolution: Build the first phase into the in-memory plan and write the file once (the body already assembles the plan under the lock), or write the empty plan to a sibling temp name and rename it only after the body returns 0.

findings.issue: The filed outcome of P123.3 ends 'Not done: the task note on whether script or model picked P1.2 ... was not established (no transcript read)'. The plan now carries a note (2026-10-11T16:32:32Z) saying it WAS established from the testbed transcript. The filed outcome therefore describes a state the record no longer has.
findings.resolution: Leave the outcome as history but make the note's provenance explicit (who read the transcript, which file), so the two statements are not left contradicting each other.

intent.note: Read against desiredOutcome clause by clause. (1) First phase in one verb call, no placeholder: P123.1 makes add-phase and add --from-file create a missing plan via _under_lock(create=True)/_create_then and gives seed --no-task; task verbs still refuse a missing plan. (2) /audit:run never runs less or more than named: P123.3 adds next --task, which raises phase_form_refusal for a phase-shaped id (one line naming /audit:phase and the tasks it would run) and picks no task; the plan note records that the script, not the model, picked P1.2. (3) A stopped drive leaves no lock: P123.2 funnels every E_STOPPED through release_lock in drive(), gives audit-task exit 3 its own followed rule, and P123.57 extends that to ValueError and any other exception raised after the lock was taken. (4) Gate evidence in the project's own directory: P123.5 sends project_config_for and run-test-gate through _output.project_of_manifest, and P123.43 later empties MANIFEST_DIRNAME_PROJECTS so every reader asks the one resolver. (5) Single-checkout landing leaves the user on the landed branch: P123.4 adds _worktrees.landing_switch (main worktree only, holds the branch, parent held nowhere, tree clean, landing run there), switches before the stamp so the stamp commits on the parent, and otherwise prints the git switch command. The remaining tasks (about 70) are hardening, lints and fixes of earlier review findings. I read the five outcome tasks' diffs in full, the later drive-phase fix, and the final commit; I did not read all of the diff across hundreds of files, and the later tasks were each reviewed by an earlier reviewer return at its own commit. No request or openChoices were saved, so the 'where a task chose what the request left open' question cannot be answered from the record.
